stances_toward.note: Gazprom holds 50% plus one share of Moldovagaz (with Transnistria 13%) and claims a debt of USD 709m, which a 2023 audit commissioned by Chișinău put at USD 8.6m. Moldova said on 2 Oct 2023 that it would stop buying Gazprom gas; Gazprom stopped deliveries on 1 Jan 2025, citing that debt. The grade is 'rival' because friction is institutional (ownership, debt, a contract valid until Oct 2026) and not directed at the firm's destruction; Moldova still depends on Moldovagaz as the legal supply channel to Transnistria. Bond - grievance: the debt dispute and the use of gas as a lever in 2022 and 2025.

stances_toward.note: SPP, the state gas company, holds a long-term supply contract with Gazprom valid to 2034 that Fico cites as proof that the EU phase-out would breach it (the contract has Gazprom bring gas to the Slovak border); after the Ukrainian transit ended on 1 Jan 2025 gas has arrived by TurkStream via Hungary. Transactional partner; cooling because volumes are capped by pipeline capacity and, per SPP's own 2025 reporting, about two-thirds of its gas came from non-Russian sources. Bond none.

A separate Stockholm (SCC) award of EUR 48m was also set off in December 2024.
